drivingQuestion: If his father has already died and left him ten thousand dinars, in what sense is the leper still destitute?
outcomeNote: R' Abbahu's emendation removes the difficulty and nothing presses further in this unit.

segments.he: אֲבָל בַּקׇּרְבָּנוֹת אֵינוֹ כֵּן וְכוּ׳. אָבִיו מֵת וְהִנִּיחַ לוֹ רִיבּוֹא — עָשִׁיר הוּא! אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, אֵימָא: מַנִּיחַ לוֹ רִיבּוֹא.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «But with regard to» the «offerings» of a leper «that is not so.» If the leper is destitute, even if his father died and left him ten thousand dinars, the Temple treasury has no share in it. The Gemara raises a difficulty: «If his father» already «died and left him ten thousand» dinars, «he is wealthy.» How could he be considered destitute at all? «Rabbi Abbahu said» that one should «say» instead: His father is dying and «leaving him ten thousand» dinars, but he has not yet died.

moves.about: quoting the mishna's clause about a leper whose father died leaving him ten thousand dinars

moves.cueHe: אָבִיו מֵת וְהִנִּיחַ לוֹ רִיבּוֹא — עָשִׁיר הוּא!
moves.summary: objects that an heir of ten thousand dinars is simply wealthy
moves.about: how a leper whose father has already died and left him ten thousand dinars can still count as destitute

moves.summary: emends the wording so the father has not yet died
moves.about: answering the difficulty by re-reading the mishna's verb so the inheritance has not yet fallen to him

edges.cueHe: אביו מת והניח לו ריבוא — עשיר הוא!
